summary.short: Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to let AI and machine learning technology qualify as a practitioner licensed to administer drugs, if a State statute authorizes it to prescribe the drug and FDA approves, clears or authorizes it under sections 510(k), 513, 515 or 564.
summary.long: The Healthy Technology Act of 2025 (bill as introduced) adds a new paragraph (6) to section 503(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The paragraph provides that the term 'practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug' includes artificial intelligence and machine learning technology that meets two conditions: (A) it is authorized under a statute of the State involved to prescribe the drug involved, and (B) it is approved, cleared or authorized under section 510(k), 513, 515 or 564 of that Act. The bill addresses the prescription-drug provisions of federal law and applies nationally. It contains no effective date, no enforcement provisions and no reporting duties. The bill has the status of introduced and is pending.

notes: The operative text is SEC. 2 only, which adds paragraph (6) to FD&C Act section 503(b). The new paragraph extends the term 'practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug' to AI and machine learning technology that is (A) authorized under a State statute to prescribe the drug and (B) approved, cleared or authorized under FD&C Act sections 510(k), 513, 515 or 564. Those sections are cited but not reproduced in the bill. The long title refers to 'other purposes', but the text contains no provisions beyond SEC. 1 (short title) and SEC. 2. The target_instrument_id is left empty because the FD&C Act is not identified in the registry.
